TIL The worlds largest salt mine is in Goderich, Ontario. It has produced over 150 million tonnes of salt to date!

An interesting tidbit of knowledge comes about when you combine this article with the previous one where the NOAA explains why oceans are salty. From the NOAA article:

"The concentration of salt in seawater (salinity) is about 35 parts per thousand. Stated in another way, about 3.5 percent of the weight of seawater comes from the dissolved salts; in a cubic mile of seawater, the weight of the salt (in the form of sodium chloride) would be about 120 million tons."

The total salt production of the Goderich, ON mine is 150 million tonnes (metric tons). The weight of salt in one cubic mile of seawater is 120 million tons (short tons) or approximately 108.862 million tonnes. If I did my math correctly, the equivalent amount of salt mined to date could be found in approximately 1.38 cubic miles of seawater containing 106,257,804,719,468 gallons of seawater. Of course the salts in seawater are not composed of only sodium chloride, so this is still pretty rough in accuracy and my calculations might not be worth their salt. Also, I'm not really sure where I'm going with this other than it seemed interesting that the two articles fit together.
